ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The same DNA fragment was treated separately with two restriction endonucleases, XhoⅠ and SalⅠ. The enzyme cutting sites and the enzyme cutting sites and the separation results of the digestion products are shown in the figure. Question: Which lane is the digestion product obtained by treatment with SalⅠ?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The restriction enzyme cutting site diagram above shows that on the same linear DNA fragment, XhoⅠ sites are located near the two ends; there are multiple SalⅠ sites, distributed inside the DNA fragment. The electrophoresis diagram below has two lanes: in lane ①, multiple bands can be seen, and the bands are relatively dispersed; lane ② mainly shows one large-fragment band near the top and a smaller-fragment band near the bottom. Reasoning: Restriction endonucleases cut only at the corresponding recognition sites, and the number and sizes of fragments produced after linear DNA is cut depend on the number and positions of the restriction sites of that enzyme. There are more SalⅠ sites, which will produce multiple small and medium fragments, so the electrophoresis result should show multiple bands; XhoⅠ sites are mainly near the two ends, which better fits an electrophoresis pattern producing one larger middle fragment and smaller end fragments. Comparing the lanes in the figure, lane ① conforms to the characteristics of SalⅠ digestion products.
